wiki_text: In August 2017 Summit signed a 15-year charter agreement with Excelerate Energy for the FSRU vessel 'Summit LNG'. In addition to chartering the vessel, Excelerate acted as Owner's Engineer for Summit on the fixed infrastructure (subsea plug, mooring system, subsea pipeline). This is a vessel-charter + engineering-services relationship, not an ownership stake -- Summit LNG Terminal Co Pvt Ltd (now with Mitsubishi Corp holding 25%, see updates.json) remains the terminal Owner/Operator of record; Excelerate is neither Owner nor Operator here (contrast with Moheshkhali, where Excelerate IS the current Owner/Operator under a build-own-operate-transfer structure).

Within roughly one month in October 2024, Bangladesh's interim government/Petrobangla cancelled or confirmed the cancellation of three separate LNG import projects covered by this scope: Payra FSRU (Excelerate bid terminated, reported 2024-10-16), Summit Matarbari FSRU (3rd FSRU deal terminated by notice dated 2024-10-07, later disputed by Summit), and RPGCL's shortlist of prequalified bidders for the Matarbari onshore LNG terminal (cancelled ~2024-10-08/09). This appears to be a coordinated policy retrenchment on new LNG import capacity under the interim administration rather than three unrelated project failures -- useful context for interpreting any single cancellation in isolation.

Moheshkhali is a BOOT project: Excelerate Energy owns/develops/operates the FSRU for a 15-year period from commissioning (Aug 2018), after which ownership transfers to Petrobangla (Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corp) -- i.e. an expected transfer around 2033. This sweep corrected GEM's Owner/Operator fields (previously showing Petrobangla, the eventual/future owner) to Excelerate (the current owner) -- see updates.json. Flagging the ~2033 transfer date so a future sweep knows to flip Owner/Operator back to Petrobangla around then.
